mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over two consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises by >0.25% in two consecutive monthly releases
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) in periods where FEDFUNDS rises by >0.25% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in Real Personal Consumption Expenditures (RSAFS) exceeding 2% coincident with a decline in Housing Starts (HOUST) signals weakening consumer demand, which reduces corporate revenue growth and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS YoY < -2% AND HOUST falls for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the correlation between the trigger and returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained acceleration in Industrial Production (INDPRO) above its 12-month moving average by more than 1.5% for two consecutive months signals a strengthening manufacturing sector, which boosts earnings expectations and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.10) during periods when INDPRO is above its 12-month moving average by >1.5% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly unemployment rate (UNRATE) falling below 4% while payroll employment (PAYEMS) rises by more than 1% month-over-month signals a tight labor market, which increases wage pressure and cost of capital, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days as markets anticipate margin compression.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) in triggered episodes, or the trigger fires but returns are positive in more than 50% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid decline in CPIAUCSL (Consumer Price Index) below 2% while FEDFUNDS remains above 4.5% for three consecutive months signals a disinflationary environment with restrictive monetary policy, which depresses risk assets and yields negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL < 2% AND FEDFUNDS > 4.5% for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) during such episodes, or the trigger is not predictive out-of-sample.

mechanism_narrative: A sequential decline in both Real Personal Consumption Expenditures (RSAFS) and Housing Starts (HOUST) for four consecutive months signals a deepening housing and consumption downturn, which reduces corporate revenues and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS and HOUST both decline for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) in triggered episodes, or the trigger produces a false-positive rate exceeding 40%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in PAYEMS above 200,000 for five consecutive months signals robust labor market expansion, which boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.10) during periods when PAYEMS exceeds 200,000 for five straight months.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly acceleration in Industrial Production (INDPRO) above its 6-month moving average by more than 2% while GDP growth (GDPC1 YoY) remains below 2% signals a supply-side recovery decoupled from broad demand, which can create volatility but ultimately supports positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days due to earnings upgrades in cyclical sectors.
regime_hint: supply recovery with weak aggregate demand
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.10) in triggered episodes, or the interaction effect is not statistically robust (p > 0.05 in regression).
